page.layout: Two engraved medallions at the top, side by side, centred. Below them one column of text with two paragraphs, the second starting at a line ending well short of the margin. A printer's ornament at the foot of the column. No catchword or signature.

main_text.l: RVDOLPHVS, Comes Habispur-
gius, Imperator eligitur anno mundi 5234. à Christo nato
1272. Interregnum imperij à deturbato Friderico per 26. an-
nos durauit. Hic Othocarum Bohemiæ Regem acie victũ oc-
cidit: Pfeudofridericum qui se in Sueuis erexerat, combusit.
In Italiam non est profectus Rudolphus, solitus Æsopi fabulâ
recitare de Vulpe, & Leone in spelunca ægrotante, apud se re-
putans maiores suos ingressos quidem sæpe magnis copiis
Italiam, sed male acceptos demum plerunque rediisse. Hic re-
dacta sub ditionem Austria, constituit in ea Ducem filium
suum Albertum, à quo originem trahunt Austriaci principes,
ad Carolum quintum usque, & Ferdinandum eius fratrem.
Vuenceslao Othocari filio, Bohemiæ regnũ, humanitate sum-
ma usus Rudolphus, reliquit, dedítque ei in uxorẽ filiã suam.
Imperat annis 19.
ADOLPHVS post Rudolphum imperat anno mundi
5253. à Christo nato 1291. Hic Comes de Naffau cũm esset,
Imperator eligitur. Sed ab electoribus pertræsis[?] eius fordes ac
ambitionem, imperio destituitur, in cuius locum subrogatur
Albertus Austriæ Dux, ac Rudolphi frater: cum quo dum con-
greditur Adolphus, occumbit anno imperij 7. Consulito Aem.
lib.8. Egna. lib.3.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions at the top: the left one shows a bearded emperor in a crown with the legend "IMP RVDOLPHVS AVGVS"; the right one shows a laureate head in profile with the legend "IMP ADOLPHVS AVG". Doubtful: "pertræsis" in the second paragraph. Printed "Pfeudofridericum" and "Vuenceslao" kept as printed. Long s is printed as f or s in several words and is given here as s.
